description: A project's rate is its total gbsize divided by its total spanmin.

c.request: Using only scans that match a project, what's each project's size-per-minute rate (`gbsize` per `spanmin`), grouped by project reference (`scans.arcref`) and funding source (`fundflux`)? Take the plain average of those project rates as a benchmark, with each project counting once. Show the 10 projects furthest above it, keeping only those strictly above, with project reference, funding source, rate and the gap above the benchmark, biggest gap first. Leave values unrounded. A project's rate is its total gbsize divided by its total spanmin.
c.sql: WITH project_rates AS (SELECT s.arcref AS project_reference, p.fundflux AS funding_source, SUM(s.gbsize) / NULLIF(SUM(s.spanmin), 0) AS rate FROM scans AS s JOIN projects AS p ON p.arcregistry = s.arcref GROUP BY s.arcref, p.fundflux), benchmark AS (SELECT AVG(rate) AS average_rate FROM project_rates) SELECT pr.project_reference, pr.funding_source, pr.rate, pr.rate - b.average_rate AS gap_above_benchmark FROM project_rates AS pr CROSS JOIN benchmark AS b WHERE pr.rate > b.average_rate ORDER BY gap_above_benchmark DESC LIMIT 10

b.request: For each project with matching scans, group by `scans.arcref` and funding source, calculate its rate as `SUM(gbsize) / SUM(spanmin)`, and compare it with the unweighted average of those project rates. Return the 10 projects strictly above that average, showing project reference, funding source, unrounded rate, and unrounded gap, ordered by largest gap first
b.sql: WITH project_rates AS (SELECT s.arcref, p.fundflux, SUM(s.gbsize) / NULLIF(SUM(s.spanmin), 0) AS rate FROM scans AS s JOIN projects AS p ON p.arcregistry = s.arcref GROUP BY s.arcref, p.fundflux), compared AS (SELECT arcref, fundflux, rate, AVG(rate) OVER () AS average_rate FROM project_rates) SELECT arcref AS project_reference, fundflux AS funding_source, rate, rate - average_rate AS gap FROM compared WHERE rate > average_rate ORDER BY gap DESC LIMIT 10

a.request: Match each scan to its project by project ID, dropping scans with no matching project, and group by project reference (`scans.arcref`) and funding source (`fundflux`). Compute each group's size-per-minute rate as its total file size (`gbsize`) divided by its total scan duration (`spanmin`). Use the simple average of these group rates as a benchmark. For groups whose rate is strictly above the benchmark, list the project reference, funding source, rate, and how much the rate exceeds the benchmark. Sort by that excess from largest to smallest and show only the top 10. Don't round.
a.sql: WITH group_rates AS (SELECT s.arcref, p.fundflux, SUM(s.gbsize) / NULLIF(SUM(s.spanmin), 0) AS rate FROM scans AS s JOIN projects AS p ON p.arcregistry = s.arcref GROUP BY s.arcref, p.fundflux), benchmark AS (SELECT AVG(rate) AS average_rate FROM group_rates) SELECT g.arcref, g.fundflux, g.rate, g.rate - b.average_rate AS excess FROM group_rates AS g CROSS JOIN benchmark AS b WHERE g.rate > b.average_rate ORDER BY excess DESC LIMIT 10

d.request: Using only scans that match a project, calculate each project’s size-per-minute rate as its total `gbsize` divided by its total `spanmin`, grouped by project reference (`scans.arcref`) and funding source (`fundflux`). Use the plain average of those project rates as the benchmark, counting each project once. Show the 10 projects strictly above the benchmark with the largest gaps, ordered by gap descending. Include the project reference, funding source, rate, and gap above the benchmark. Leave values unrounded.
d.sql: WITH project_rates AS (SELECT s.arcref, p.fundflux, SUM(s.gbsize) / NULLIF(SUM(s.spanmin), 0) AS rate FROM scans AS s JOIN projects AS p ON p.arcregistry = s.arcref GROUP BY s.arcref, p.fundflux), benchmark AS (SELECT AVG(rate) AS avg_rate FROM project_rates) SELECT pr.arcref, pr.fundflux, pr.rate, pr.rate - b.avg_rate AS gap FROM project_rates AS pr CROSS JOIN benchmark AS b WHERE pr.rate > b.avg_rate ORDER BY gap DESC LIMIT 10;
